name: Stephen
role: One of the Seven, the first Christian martyr
whenBasis: The first years of the Jerusalem church, between the crucifixion (AD 30 or 33) and Saul's conversion, which Paul's own reckoning (Galatians 1:18; 2:1) and the Gallio date put ≈AD 33–35.
summary: One of the seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom chosen to oversee the daily distribution to widows, a man full of faith, grace and power, who performed great wonders among the people. Men from the Synagogue of the Freedmen could not stand up to his wisdom, so they brought false witnesses who said he spoke against the temple and the Law. Before the council he retold Israel's history, from Abraham to Solomon's temple, and charged them with resisting the Holy Spirit as their fathers had. He saw heaven open and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand. They dragged him out and stoned him; he prayed for his killers as he died, and a young man named Saul approved.
body: The council sees that his face is like the face of an angel. His last words are “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” and “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” The witnesses lay their garments at Saul's feet. Devout men bury him, and the persecution that follows scatters the church through Judea and Samaria.

moments.text: Full of faith and the Holy Spirit
“Do not hold this sin against them”

later.text: A priest named Lucian wrote that in AD 415 a dream led him to Stephen's relics at Kefar Gamala; they were brought to Jerusalem, and a basilica was later built north of the city where he was thought to have been stoned.

sources.title: Lucian of Caphargamala, Letter on the Discovery of the Body of Saint Stephen (415)
